releases.notes:
Codex in the notch, a welcome tour you can finish before Claude Code is installed, and a tidier installer.

- **Codex agents, beside Claude's.** The Agents tab has a Claude | Codex switch at its top. Codex agents show the same statuses, raise the same banners and play the same sounds, and the Codex side shows Codex's own 5-hour and weekly figures. Connect it once with the command in Settings → Codex. Codex approvals can be allowed or denied from the notch.
- **Set up later.** The welcome tour no longer insists on a Claude Code folder. On a Mac without Claude Code yet, choose Set up later and finish the tour. Cloud Notch finds `~/.claude` by itself once Claude Code is installed, with nothing to restart. Until then the Agents tab says it is waiting, with a Set up button for a folder somewhere else.
- **A proper install window.** The disk image opens to a window that shows the app, an arrow and the Applications folder, with nothing else in the way.

A record player in the Media tab, and a simpler Shelf.

- **The Media tab is a record player.** What is playing is now a record that turns slowly, with the artwork as its label. It stops where it is when you pause. Beside it are a playing lamp, a line with a knob to drag to seek, and three round keys for previous, play or pause, and next. The record grows as you make the panel bigger, and holds still if Reduce Motion is on.
- **The Shelf has one place to drop.** The whole tab keeps whatever you drop on it, and lights up orange while you drag over it. It is no longer split into a side that keeps and a side that sends, so a file can't go to AirDrop by landing in the wrong half.
- **AirDrop from the list.** Every item on the Shelf now shows its AirDrop button all the time, not only under the pointer. Click an item to open it, or drag it back out, as before.

The first version you download from the website, instead of the Mac App Store.

- **Direct download.** Cloud Notch now comes as a disk image, signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Open it and drag the app to Applications.
- **Tells you when there is an update.** Once a day the app checks whether a newer version is out. When one is, a blue arrow appears in the notch's tab bar, and Settings → General shows what is new with a Download button. Nothing is installed for you, and the check can be turned off.
- **Live plan usage is now your choice.** It is off until you turn it on, in the welcome tour or in Settings → Plan Figures. Turned on, Cloud Notch uses the login Claude Code keeps in your Keychain to ask Anthropic for your 5-hour and weekly figures, as before. Off, it reads no login and sends nothing, and the notch shows the figures Claude Code saves itself. If you used live figures before, turn them on again once; the notch has a "Show live usage" link for it.
